facts.text: The brown falcon is a relatively large falcon native to Australia and New Guinea.
facts.quote: The brown falcon (Falco berigora) is a relatively large falcon native to Australia and New Guinea.

facts.text: Brown falcons come in pale and dark plumage forms, both usually with dark brown upper parts and wing coverts.
facts.quote: A number of plumage morphs occur, with the primary distinction being between the pale morph and the dark morph. Both morphs usually have dark brown upper parts and wing coverts.

facts.text: Pale morph birds have white underparts streaked with brown, and prominently white under tail coverts may be diagnostic.
facts.quote: Pale morph birds have white underparts that are varyingly streaked with brown, sometimes heavily so. Pale individuals may also have prominently white under tail coverts and these may be diagnostic.

facts.text: In the breeding season, brown falcons make a loud, high pitched cackle call, like a laying hen, while in flight.
facts.quote: A distinctive aspect of their behaviour is shown in the breeding season when brown falcons make a loud, high pitched, cackle call (like a laying hen) and screeching while in flight.

facts.text: The species name berigora has Aboriginal origins.
facts.quote: The species name berigora has Aboriginal origins.

facts.text: Brown falcons and other Australian firehawks have been said to pick up burning sticks and drop them to spread fires and prey on escaping animals.
facts.quote: Brown falcons and other Australian firehawks have been said to pick up sticks with flames and dropping them to spread fires and prey on escaping animals.

facts.text: The brown falcon eats small mammals including house mice and young rabbits in summer, plus small birds, lizards and snakes.
facts.quote: The brown falcon eats small mammals, including house mice. They also eat young rabbits in the summer. It also eats small birds, lizards, snakes, and a variety of invertebrates

facts.text: In winter, insects form the bulk of the brown falcon's diet, and it often chases them on the ground.
facts.quote: Insects form the bulk of the animals' diets during winter and the falcons often chase the insects on the ground.

facts.text: Brown falcons breed from June to November, usually in an old nest of a larger passerine or another hawk, sometimes in a tree hollow.
facts.quote: Brown falcons breed from June to November, usually in an old nest of a larger passerine or another hawk species; they occasionally nest in hollow limbs of trees.

facts.text: The brown falcon lays two to five eggs with red and brown spots and blotches.
facts.quote: The brown falcon lays between two and five eggs that have red and brown spots and blotches.
